title: California subpoenas OpenAI over cybersecurity incidents and model risks
friendlyTitle: California is asking OpenAI detailed questions about AI security
summary: California Attorney General Rob Bonta served OpenAI with an investigative subpoena as part of a broader inquiry into cybersecurity incidents and risks involving the company and its models. The action follows a state investigation into an incident involving Hugging Face and asks whether model developers met their legal responsibilities.
friendlySummary: California’s Attorney General sent OpenAI a legal demand for information about cybersecurity incidents and risks linked to its models.
whyItMatters: Regulators are moving from general AI principles toward examining specific incidents, controls and accountability. Businesses deploying frontier models should retain incident records, define who owns model-related security risk and avoid assuming that responsibility sits only with the model provider.
friendlyWhyItMatters: AI security is becoming a legal and operational issue. Businesses should keep good records and clearly assign responsibility when they use powerful models.
